🪄 ONNX Simplifier — Constant Folding & Subgraph Elimination

Many exported networks compute values at runtime that could be resolved at build time. A chain of ops on constant tensors runs every inference — wasting both intermediate memory and node count.

onnxsim fixes this by actually running the graph, identifying subgraphs with constant outputs, and replacing them with their precomputed results.

What it catches:
📐 Constant folding — subgraphs fed only by initializers get collapsed into a single Constant
🚫 Redundant ops — Identity, no-op Reshape, Cast-to-same-type, Transpose with identity permutation
🔗 Shape simplification — Shape→Gather→Concat chains resolved to static values

Why it matters for NeuroGolf:
Every eliminated intermediate tensor saves num_elements × dtype_size bytes from the memory cost. Fewer nodes = fewer intermediates = lower cost = higher score.

cost = total_parameters + total_memory_in_bytes
score = max(1, 25 - ln(cost))

Same outputs. Smaller graph. Higher score. 🎯

📜 onnxscript Optimizer — IR-Level Graph Rewriting

Microsoft's onnxscript.optimizer operates on ONNX's intermediate representation directly — a different engine from onnxsim, catching redundancies left behind.

It runs multiple iterations: each pass can expose new opportunities for the next — a constant fold reveals a no-op, the no-op removal reveals a dead branch, and so on.

What it catches:
🔄 Iterative constant folding — multi-pass: fold → simplify → fold again until nothing changes
💀 Dead code elimination — nodes whose outputs feed nothing get removed along with their intermediates
🧩 Shape-aware rewrites — leverages full shape inference to resolve dynamic-looking patterns into static ones

Why stack it after onnxsim:
Different optimization engines have different blind spots. Running onnxsim first handles the bulk; onnxscript then sweeps for what remains — often shaving a few more intermediate tensors that translate directly to memory savings.

Same outputs. Cleaner graph. Higher score. 🎯

📜 onnxscript Optimizer — IR-Level Graph Rewriting

Microsoft's onnxscript.optimizer operates on ONNX's intermediate representation directly — a different engine from onnxsim, catching redundancies left behind.

It runs multiple iterations: each pass can expose new opportunities for the next — a constant fold reveals a no-op, the no-op removal reveals a dead branch, and so on.

What it catches:
🔄 Iterative constant folding — multi-pass: fold → simplify → fold again until nothing changes
💀 Dead code elimination — nodes whose outputs feed nothing get removed along with their intermediates
🧩 Shape-aware rewrites — leverages full shape inference to resolve dynamic-looking patterns into static ones

Why stack it after onnxsim:
Different optimization engines have different blind spots. Running onnxsim first handles the bulk; onnxscript then sweeps for what remains — often shaving a few more intermediate tensors that translate directly to memory savings.

Same outputs. Cleaner graph. Higher score. 🎯
